pageCache.pageTitle: Badminton Clubs Take off at Longhill Sports Centre - Longhill High School
pageCache.text:
Latest News
Badminton Clubs Take off at Longhill Sports Centre
Posted in: Latest News
At the start of this year, staff at Longhill Sports Centre (LSC) decided to add badminton to their list of activities and academies on offer. Now, six months later, the shuttlecocks are still flying, with the badminton clubs going from strength to strength.
Longhill Sports Centre’s Junior Badminton Academy runs every Tuesday from 5 – 6pm and takes players of all levels, aged between 5 and 12 years. Working alongside Darren Hambrook, from the Deans Sports Partnership, the junior academy is proving very popular amongst local primary school children. The cost is great value, at £20 for a 6-week course.
The young players enjoyed recent success in the Rising Stars Junior Tournament, organised by Sussex County Junior Badminton. Junior players may wish to go along to their under 12 badminton festival on Saturday 7th July at Portslade Sports Centre from 2-4 pm. County coaches will lead an afternoon of activities for children with an interest in badminton and it’s free of charge.
Badminton has long been a popular sport amongst adults too and the classes at LSC have produced some very promising players, both in the beginners and intermediate/advanced classes. Both classes run on Wednesday evenings from 8-9pm and 9-10pm respectively and have the benefit of Badminton England coaches.
Adult players are really keen to get competitive and the plan is to launch several teams to compete in regional competitions throughout Sussex from September 2018.
“It’s a fantastic sport for improving fitness, stamina and for sheer enjoyment,” commented LSC Manager, Allan Parker-Read. “As a club, we are keen to raise awareness of the sport amongst adults, particularly female players, who are the most under-represented group nationally.” He added, “By this September we will be launching as many adult teams as we have players wanting to compete – and we have some very good players on our books already, but there’s always room for more.”
Perhaps you are a ‘lapsed’ player, or have always fancied trying badminton, so why not come along on Wednesday evening to the Longhill Sports Centre and give it a try? It’s just £25 for a 10-week adults’ course. The LSC coaches and staff can promise a warm welcome!
For further information about Junior or Adult Badminton Clubs, please contact Gary Dove on 01273 391683.

Careers Fair 2026
Posted in: Latest News, Transition
Last week, our school was proud to host an inspiring Careers Fair, bringing together a wide range of employers to support our students in planning their future pathways.
The event gave students the opportunity to speak directly with professionals from a variety of industries, ask questions about different career routes and gain valuable insight into the skills and qualifications needed for future success. From apprenticeships and vocational training to university courses and employment opportunities, there was something to inspire every student.
A huge thank you goes to all of the organisations and visitors who gave up their time to attend and share their expertise. Their support helped create meaningful conversations and opened our students’ eyes to the many possibilities available to them after school.
Our students represented the school brilliantly throughout the event, showing curiosity, confidence and maturity as they engaged with exhibitors and explored new opportunities.
Events like this are an important part of preparing young people for life beyond the classroom, helping them to make informed decisions and raise aspirations for the future. We look forward to continuing to build strong links with employers and education providers in the years ahead.
For more support on Careers, visit our careers page: https://longhill.org.uk/academic/careers/

pageCache.pageTitle: Real Madrid Football Clinic at Longhill Sports Centre - Longhill High School
pageCache.text:
In the Community, Latest News
Real Madrid Football Clinic at Longhill Sports Centre
Posted in: In the Community, Latest News
On Monday 11th August, our sports centre was buzzing with excitement as we proudly hosted a Real Madrid Football Clinic coaching session making it an unforgettable experience for young football enthusiasts and aspiring athletes alike.
This isn’t the first time we’ve had the honour of collaborating with Real Madrid C.F.—and each time, the excitement and energy on the pitch remind us why we continue to bring this opportunity to our community.
The event brought the magic of one of the world’s most iconic football clubs right to our doorstep. Led by certified coaches from the Real Madrid Foundation, the clinic offered participants a taste of elite-level training, focusing on technical skills, teamwork, and the values that define the beautiful game.
Throughout the day, students were immersed in high-energy drills, tactical exercises, and motivational talks that emphasized discipline, respect, and sportsmanship. Each session was tailored to age and skill level, ensuring every player had the chance to grow and shine.
This summer’s clinic was made even more special thanks to our partnership with Woodingdean Wanderers Football Club and the Woodingdean Wanderers Wildcats. Together, we created a vibrant and inclusive environment where aspiring footballers could sharpen their skills, build confidence, and experience the magic of training under the Real Madrid banner.
We’re proud to say that Longhill High School continues to live by its motto: “In the community, for the community.”
Longhill High School is proud to be home to Longhill Sports Centre—a vibrant hub offering top-tier facilities that support both student development and community wellbeing. Whether you’re into football, gymnastics, badminton, or simply staying active, the centre provides a welcoming space that prioritises health, fitness, and connection.
Discover everything it has to offer by visiting the Longhill Sports Centre website.

Brighton Bowmen Host Sussex County Indoors Championships 2025
Posted in: In the Community, Latest News
On 25/26 January 2025, Brighton Bowmen hosted the Sussex County Indoors Championships for archery, for the third year running, at Longhill Sports Centre. 136 archers gathered from across the county and beyond, from 10 years old upwards towards retired.
Their skills ranged from beginners to former Olympic archers in attendance. Longhill’s facilities are great for accessibility purposes, with the accessibility parking spaces, toilets and ramps around the centre to access all areas.
Archers wanting to shoot here can easily find their way as the site is accessible by public transport from Brighton – the journey takes approximately 30 minutes from the town centre. If you are interested in archery, please contact Brighton Bowmen via brightonbowmen@gmail.com and they will happily contact you to provide further information.
Photo credits go to Andy Pelling, talented sports photographer.

pageCache.pageTitle: Longhill CCF: War Memorial Rededication & Service - Longhill High School
pageCache.text:
In the Community, Latest News, Spotlight
Longhill CCF: War Memorial Rededication & Service
Posted in: In the Community, Latest News, Spotlight
Longhill Cadets were kindly invited by the Mayor of Brighton and Hove to take part in the Rededication of the newly renovated War Memorial at Stein Gardens. This was initiated by Paul Tilley of our premises staff who is also the chairman of the Brighton and Hove Veterans. We thank Paul for his support of the contingent and proposing us for this honour.
This was of particular importance to Longhill CCF as we are currently the only uniformed unit to still wear the Royal Sussex Regiment cap badge. We were given this honour back in 1986 by the Royal Sussex Regiment Association and one we are very proud of. The service was also attended by members of the Royal Sussex Regimental Association.
The Battle of Boar’s Head, often overshadowed by the more infamous Battle of the Somme, was a tragic and significant event during the First World War, particularly for the communities of Sussex. Fought on 30 June 1916, it served as a diversionary tactic aimed at drawing German forces away from the Somme, set to commence the following day.
The Battle of Boar’s Head was disastrous: 366 soldiers were killed, and over 1000 were wounded or missing, many of whom were later confirmed as prisoners of war. This calamity had a profound impact on Sussex, with 70% of those killed being natives of the region. The heavy losses led to the day being remembered locally as “The Day Sussex Died.”
The communities of Brighton, Hove, and Portslade were particularly hard hit, with over 850 men from these areas enlisted in the South Downs Battalions. The grief permeated through entire communities, affecting not just families but friends, colleagues, and neighbours. Areas such as east Brighton, the Hanover area, and Poets’ Corner in Hove were especially impacted.
The event was hosted by The Right Worshipful Mayor of Brighton and Hove Councillor Theresa Fowler and the Service was conducted by Archdeacon of Brighton & Lewes; The Venerable Martin Lloyd Williams & The Mayor’s Chaplain; The Reverend Tom Holbird.
Also in attendance was Major General John Moore-Bick CBE DL on behalf of HM Lord-Lieutenant of East Sussex.
After the service, wreaths were laid by Major General John Moore-Bick CBE DL, the Mayor of Brighton & Hove, members of The Royal Sussex Regimental Association, together with other invited dignitaries and members of the public.
The ceremony culminated with the Exhortation, the playing of The Last Post, the Kohima Epitaph and a blessing.
Afterwards we were invited by the Mayor for tea and cake in the Mayoral Chambers.
The next day we received some kind words from the Mayor:
“We received many positive comments about how smart, professional, and dedicated the cadets appeared, and it was especially appreciated to see them join us, given the strong connection with the Royal Sussex Regiment. Major General John Moore-Bick was also highly complementary”.
Longhill CCF Contingent Commander.
Read more from Longhill High School: https://longhill.org.uk/news/

Results Day 2026
Posted in: Education, In the Community, Latest News, Spotlight, Transition
Secondary Headteachers across Brighton & Hove are writing jointly to celebrate the achievements of our students and recognise the hard work, determination and resilience that has brought them to this point. As a city, we believe every young person is a City Child, and that every child’s success matters to us all. Today’s results reflect the achievements of individual students and the dedication of the staff, families and communities who support them.
We also recognise that every school serves a unique community, with different cohorts of young people bringing their own experiences, strengths and challenges. Results are only one part of the story of a school and the young people within it. Our shared commitment is to celebrate success wherever it is found, learn from one another and continue working together to ensure that every City Child has the opportunity to thrive. We are incredibly proud of all our students, congratulate them on their achievements and wish them every success for the future.
We are immensely proud of the hard work and determination our students have shown throughout their GCSE and BTEC courses, and we wish them the very best as they take their next steps.

The school’s method of payment is online via ParentPay. All parents/carers are provided with a ParentPay account number when your child starts at the school and payment is quick and easy to set up.
Paying online means that you avoid having to send in cheques, or you or your child bringing cash into school. ParentPay is a secure online payment system that can be used to pay for school trips, lunches and any other expenses that may be incurred at school.
If you need assistance setting up ParentPay or have misplaced the ParentPay account number please email admin@longhill.org.uk and we will be pleased to help you.
Frequently asked questions
How Do I Activate My Account?
To create a new account, you will need to have the account activation letter provided by the school to hand. You will also need to be able to access your email as your email address will become your new username and is used for the verification process.
If you have lost your activation letter or have not yet received it, please get in touch with the school admin@longhill.org.uk.
Why Have I Not Received My Verification Email?
Some email providers may move ParentPay password verification emails to a spam or junk folder. If you have requested password verification and the email has not arrived please check those folders.
Gmail account holders, please also check the ‘All’ and ‘Promotions’ inboxes.
If you still have not received the verification email please contact ParentPay here.
Will Longhill High School continue to use ParentPay?
Yes, we will. Longhill High School now uses a totally cashless system for all school payments – this includes lunches, trips and any other expenses that may occur. ParentPay is easy to use, safe and avoids the need to bring cash to school.
Please be assured that help is available if you need it. For any queries about ParentPay, please email us at cashless@longhill.org.uk
